thread:
Ben S: FYI -- Acme sent back the CAIQ with a bunch of 'shared' controls. They asked for a clear ownership matrix. Can we align on what we mark as Provider vs Customer?
Maya P: Thanks. Top concerns from their sec team: KMS/BYOK, VPC isolation, log retention & access, incident runbook responsibilities.
Cindy R: I'll draft recommended answers. Quick notes: for CAIQ items about 'key management' we should differentiate platform keys vs customer-managed keys. If customer uses BYOK, ownership shifts.
Alex T: Agreed. For Hosted API customers (default) we should mark: Provider = key rotation for platform keys; Customer = guest/tenant-level keys if they upload their own.
Ben S: Can we put that in the CAIQ text so the vendor reviewer doesn't press back? They asked for exact wording they can paste into their intake form.
Cindy R: Draft wording below — feel free to copy: 

`Encryption (Data at Rest): Redwood Inference encrypts customer data at rest using platform-managed keys (AES-256). Customers may opt to use customer-managed keys (BYOK) via supported KMS integrations; when BYOK is enabled, key lifecycle (generation, rotation, destruction) is the customer's responsibility. Redwood enforces access controls and audit logging on platform keys and does not export customer plaintext to third parties.`

Cindy R: For network controls: 
`Network Isolation: Hosted customers are served from isolated tenant namespaces within shared VPCs and logical isolation at the application level. Dedicated and Private deployments provide customer-dedicated VPCs and/or on-premise networking; networking configuration and egress firewall rules are the customer's responsibility in those deployments.`

Alex T: For logging / retention: we can state default retention and options: logs retained 90 days by default, can extend with Enterprise plan (configurable up to X days). Access to logs is role-based; we provide export tools.
Maya P: They also asked about incident response — who runs the postmortem and who notifies customers?
Cindy R: Standard: Provider is responsible for platform-level incident detection and remediation. For customer-impacting incidents, Redwood will notify affected customers per the SLA (email + console alert) and coordinate post-incident reports. Customer is responsible for their application-level forensic actions and internal notifications.
Ben S: Perfect. Can you add a short table line we can paste for each 'shared' control? They want 1-2 sentences per control.
Cindy R: Sure — adding quick paste-ready lines: 
- `KMS / Key Management`: Provider: platform keys (rotation/backup) — Customer: BYOK lifecycle and access controls when enabled.
- `Network / Isolation`: Provider: logical isolation, routing controls; Customer: VPC peering, security groups, and on-prem firewall config for Private deployments.
- `Logging & Monitoring`: Provider: collect platform logs, offer RBAC access; Customer: retain and manage application logs and alerts; configure forwarding to their SIEM if desired.
- `Incident Response`: Provider: detect, mitigate platform incidents, and provide post-incident reports; Customer: manage application-specific remediation and regulatory notifications.

SecurityBot: CAIQ draft snippet uploaded to /shared/caiq/1769458123-acme-draft.md (automated).

LegalBot: Quick reminder — don't commit to specific retention windows or SLA terms in CAIQ answers unless Product has approved. Keep phrasing "default" and "configurable via Enterprise plan".

Alex T: Updated wording to avoid hard numbers, swapped 90 days -> "default 90 days (configurable under Enterprise plan)" per Legal.
Maya P: I'll send this to Acme's security reviewer now, include the uploaded draft link. Ben — can you CC the AE in the thread?
Ben S: Will do. Thanks everyone, sending now. :thumbsup:
Alex T: If they push back on BYOK details, escalate to Cindy and Legal and we'll provide the BYOK integration docs.
Cindy R: I'll stand by for follow-up.
Ben S: Thread closed after I confirm customer receipt (I'll update TS).
